inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (59.910M, Class A+B+C+D combined). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and buybacks (FY25 $968M, H1-26 $485M) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat, so they are value-neutral here. Period-end count is somewhat lower after Q2's $320M repurchase, so this divisor is mildly conservative.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement ShareBasedCompensation add-back ($95.688M, SEC XBRL companyfacts). Cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not separately tagged (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation absent); UHS publishes no combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line, so the add-back alone is used. Understates true SBC cost by an immaterial amount (SBC is ~0.55% of revenue).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Cost of equity 10.0% = 4.2% 10y UST + beta ~1.15 x 5.0% ERP. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (FY25 interest expense $156M on ~$5.0-5.5B average debt) -> 4.0% after tax at 24%. Market-value weights ~66% equity ($10.5B at the current price) / 34% debt ($5.5B) -> 8.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: policy, litigation and volume risk are carried in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not in a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: lease cost (~$102M FY25) already sits inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is post-lease (treatment B equivalent). Operating lease liabilities ($414M at FY25) are EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings incl. finance leases from the balance sheet. lease_cost_pct_path = 0 because the charge is already in the margin.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are whole-company (pre-NCI). NCI is small (FY25 NCI share of net income $22.4M, ~1.5% of group NI), so it is deducted once as a stock in the equity bridge: equity NCI $67.8M + redeemable NCI $74.0M at 2026-06-30. No NCI leakage in the flows.
inputs.ebitda_definition: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC EBITDA: XBRL operating income + D&A + SBC. FY25: 1,994.0 + 618.7 + 95.7 = 2,708.4 (15.60% of revenue); H1-26: 15.19%. The CSV EBITDA column (2,612.8) is post-SBC; SBC is then re-charged in the engine via sbc_pct_path, so it is charged once. FY0 tie: EBIT 1,994 - interest 156 + other income ~134 = 1,972 reported pretax; at 24% tax less NCI the modelled NOPAT less after-tax interest ties to $1,511M attributable NI within ~1%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (scenario-weighted), per dcf-methods routing row 'operating company' with the adaptations for leases (US GAAP operating leases inside EBITDA, excluded from net debt) and NCI (bridge deduction). UHS is a US hospital operator (acute care ~63% of revenue, behavioral health ~37%) -- not a bank/REIT/holdco; first valuation, no prior model. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); anchors refreshed to the Q2-2026 10-Q balance sheet (debt $5,671.9M, cash $138.8M, 2026-06-30). Owner FCF FY25 = reported FCF 849.2 - SBC 95.7 - interest income 0 = $753.6M; interest income not stripped because UHS is net-debt (~2.0x EBITDA). Reported FCF is after ~$156M cash interest; the component build is unlevered (pre-interest) and debt is deducted in the bridge, so interest is charged once. Repurchaser: the flat share count is funded by actual buybacks ($968M FY25, $485M H1-26, ~$978M authorization remaining). FY2026 guidance (Q2 call, 2026-07-28): adjusted EBITDA less NCI $2.61-2.72B (cut ~$50M at midpoint for softer volumes and ~$50M higher PL/GL reserves), capex $0.95-1.10B; base year-1 margin (15.2% pre-SBC) sits at the guidance midpoint. The $535M behavioral-health jury verdict and related litigation are NOT deducted in the bridge (insurance coverage and post-trial reduction unknown from the filings available); they are carried as a bear-case margin and weight risk. Working capital: receivables-heavy, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture -6% of revenue change; FY25 AR rose $318M on $1.54B revenue growth).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (2.8%) diverges by far more than 30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (16.2%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (8.5%): UHS has retired ~25% of its share count since FY2020 ($5.5B of buybacks FY20-H1-26), so book value understates the compounding. Revenue CAGR is selected as the anchor, and the base path decelerates from 7% well below it.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF - SBC) CAGRs are uninformative: FY2020 FCF ($1.63B) is inflated by CARES Act Medicare advance payments that reversed in FY2021 (owner FCF -$46M), and FY2022 ($177M) is the repayment/labour-cost trough. SBC grew roughly in line with revenue (FY20 $65.8M -> FY25 $95.7M), so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF series do not diverge for SBC reasons; the 3yr gap (62% vs 48%) is a small-base effect off the FY22 trough. EPS CAGR is inflated by both margin recovery from the FY22 trough and buybacks.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 +7% (H1-26 +8.9% incl. Palm Beach Gardens and bed additions, H2 slower on cut volume guidance); decelerating to 3% as pricing normalises and outpatient migration caps acute admissions.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 at the FY26 guidance midpoint (~$2.67B adj. EBITDA less NCI, ~15.2% pre-SBC pre-NCI); eases to 15.0% mid-cycle as OBBBA provider-fee thresholds phase down (FFY2028-32) against operating leverage from the 2025-26 capacity build. FY17-19 averaged ~16%; FY22-23 trough ~12.5-12.8%.
base.capex_rationale: FY26 guided $0.95-1.10B (~5.4%); normalises to 5.0%, the FY2010-25 average, as the construction cycle completes (management commentary).

scenario_narratives.base: Volumes recover only modestly from the cut 2026 guidance (acute admissions +1.5-2.5%, behavioral patient days +1-2%), with revenue growth carried by pricing, acuity and the 2025-26 capacity additions (Palm Beach Gardens, 178 acute and 264 behavioral beds). Medicaid supplemental-payment pressure from the OBBBA provider-fee phase-down and higher PL/GL reserves roughly offset operating leverage, holding pre-SBC EBITDA margin near 15% mid-cycle. Capex normalises to ~5% of revenue after the construction cycle, lifting owner FCF from ~$0.75B toward ~$1.3B by the early 2030s.
scenario_narratives.bull: Behavioral health bed scarcity lets UHS keep pricing ahead of labour inflation while new de novo hospitals and freestanding EDs ramp to mature margins; Medicaid cuts are phased slowly or offset by state directed-payment programs; acute admissions return to 3%+ as the ACA-subsidy coverage shock fades. Margin rebuilds toward the FY2017-19 ~16% level and capex drops below the long-run average, converting into materially higher FCF that funds the buyback.
scenario_narratives.bear: OBBBA work requirements and provider-fee threshold cuts take Medicaid supplemental payments out of both segments from FY2028, ACA subsidy expiry raises uninsured/self-pay mix and bad debt, and behavioral-health litigation (the $535M verdict, Illinois abuse suits) brings higher liability cost and licensing/regulatory friction in the higher-margin segment. Acute volumes keep migrating to outpatient. Margin slides to 13% -- near the FY2022-23 trough -- while capex stays elevated to defend share.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because UHS itself discloses the OBBBA Medicaid changes as potentially materially adverse, management already cut 2026 guidance mid-year, and behavioral litigation is a live, unquantified liability. Base 50% reflects a steady 15% margin business with a decade of resilient earnings. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs volumes, Medicaid policy and labour costs to break favourably at the same time.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hospital operator valued on unlevered owner FCF (SBC expensed, share count flat, debt and NCI deducted once in the bridge). Value is driven by the mid-cycle EBITDA margin and capex normalisation; reimbursement policy is the dominant risk and is carried in the scenario margins and a 25% bear weight rather than in the discount rate. Terminal value capped at 12-15x FCF, below Gordon at an 8% WACC, consistent with the regulated, labour-intensive, policy-exposed character of US hospitals.
key_risks_to_valuation: Medicaid supplemental-payment cuts under OBBBA (provider-fee thresholds 6% -> 3.5% FFY2028-32) and Medicaid work requirements
Behavioral-health litigation: $535M jury verdict and further abuse/neglect suits; uninsured portion not deducted in the bridge
Labour cost inflation and PL/GL claim severity (2026 reserves +~$50M)
Acute volume migration to outpatient settings; 2026 volume guidance already cut
Capex not normalising after the build cycle would keep FCF near FY25 levels
